review_detail.rationale: The first must_include is compound. The response calls the example synthetic/invented and says it never came from a server, correctly separates estimates from observations and candidate keys from selected keys, and leaves performance gains unknown. That substantively supports candidate_pass. The criterion also expressly distinguishes an authored fixture from a model result; the response never expressly addresses the latter distinction. facts_to_verify.response_text: ANALYZE ... reports actual rows and timings.
facts_to_verify.finding: Plain tabular ANALYZE provides r_rows and r_filtered. ANALYZE FORMAT=JSON provides additional data including per-node r_total_time_ms. A client may independently show total wall time, so the broad word timings is ambiguous; do not upgrade this into a claim that all timing is impossible with plain ANALYZE.

facts_to_verify.finding: MariaDB documents ANALYZE <statement> and ANALYZE FORMAT=JSON <statement>. The JSON documentation expressly distinguishes per-node r_total_time_ms from regular tabular output. The statement documentation identifies EXPLAIN ANALYZE as a similar PostgreSQL command.

review_detail.rationale: The response supplies a 30-person menu outline, explicit portion assumptions, supplier/product questions, and current-label/professional verification. It therefore meets the stated rubric. The review flag concerns two extra domain statements: a categorical batch/pan-depth prescription and wording that can conflate lactose intolerance with milk allergy. facts_to_verify.response_text: Larger batches need longer times, deeper pans, and checks of core temperature.
facts_to_verify.finding: No primary source or kitchen process evidence in this review establishes that larger batches universally need deeper pans or longer cooking times. Recipe, equipment, batch division, geometry, and validated process can affect the answer. Do not infer a universally correct alternative pan depth from this flag.

NHS distinguishes lactose intolerance, involving a milk sugar, from food allergy. This supports clearer clinical/dietary wording. It does not alone establish a violation of jurisdiction-specific allergen-label terminology; some regulatory milk-category wording includes lactose, so do not mark the phrase categorically false from this source.

review_detail.usefulness_assessment: Menu quantities are explicitly assumptions and the response routes safety decisions to the kitchen/professional. No scoring change; the repair is to improve actionable domain accuracy.
recommended_next_action: Have a qualified foodservice reviewer check the batching sentence against the intended recipe and equipment; replace the blanket deeper-pan/time rule with a validated kitchen process.
Separate milk-allergen requirements from lactose-related dietary requirements, while retaining exact-label and supplier confirmation.
If publishing a regulatory labeling claim, obtain an official source for the relevant jurisdiction instead of inferring one from general clinical guidance.
review_detail.acceptance_evidence: Future wording should avoid a universal pan-depth prescription, keep time/yield estimates conditional, distinguish the two dietary concerns, and avoid any claim that a dish has been certified safe.
